audit_findings.title: Unreserved CAS pension investigation could create a senior cash claim
audit_findings.mechanism: Any repayment, disallowed-cost recovery, interest or civil penalty would reduce future owner earnings or require a direct deduction from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The sensitivity to changes in interest rate assumptions makes it reasonably possible the outcome of these matters could have a material adverse effect on our financial position, results of operations and/or cash flows, although we are not currently able to estimate a range of any potential loss.
audit_findings.explanation: No loss is accrued or estimable. The DOJ criminal inquiry closed in May 2026, but the civil investigative demand and DCMA inquiry remain unresolved, and the latest filing continues to state that the outcome could materially affect financial position, earnings or cash flow. This is an unresolved material possibility, not a demonstrated valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the latest DCMA determination, civil-CID status, claimed cost differential, applicable interest and penalties, management exposure scenarios and any post-quarter accrual; rerun with a probability-weighted equity deduction or recurring OE adjustment.

audit_findings.title: Uncertain tax positions are omitted from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $2.031 billion of latest gross UTP liabilities ($831 million current plus approximately $1.2 billion non-current), versus $962 million of taxes receivable; expected net cash exposure unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash settlements not already reflected in forecast tax expense would reduce bridge cash or require a separate equity deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we have approximately $1.6 billion in unrecognized tax benefits.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest gross UTP liabilities equal about 7.4% of the $27.359 billion base equity value, or approximately $14.23 per diluted share, before considering receivables or future tax benefits. The record does not establish how much will be paid, when it will be paid, or whether the $962 million receivable offsets the same matters, but the disclosed scale is reasonably capable of materially changing estimated value. Omission is therefore unresolved rather than a demonstrated full-liability error.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile current and non-current UTP liabilities, accrued interest and penalties, the $962 million tax receivable, deferred-tax benefits and the 2026 UTP remeasurement by tax year and issue; rerun using only expected net cash payments not captured in forecast OE.

audit_findings.title: Added investment stakes may back employee-benefit claims
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum $428 million, approximately $3.00 per diluted share and 1.6% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any securities supporting non-qualified benefits are not freely distributable stakes and should be offset against the corresponding employee-benefit claims in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The company holds a portfolio of marketable securities including investments to partially fund non-qualified employee benefit plans as well as investments in companies that are advancing or developing technologies applicable to our business.
audit_findings.explanation: The asset-purpose issue is unresolved, but even removing the entire $428 million stakes adjustment would reduce each scenario by only about $3.00 per share, including base value from $191.71 to about $188.71. That bounded maximum is too small to alter the valuation conclusion, although it should be corrected if restricted amounts are identified.
audit_findings.action: Trace every component of stakes_net to the latest marketable-securities schedule and non-qualified-plan funding records; offset identified plan-backed assets and confirm that any remaining amount is distributable surplus.

audit_findings.title: FAS/CAS pension accounting could contaminate the owner-earnings numerator
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 filed non-operating FAS pension benefit of $541 million plus $527 million MTM benefit equals $1.068 billion; CAS expense was $475 million and contributions were $130 million; exact OE error unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Unsustainable FAS pension benefits or MTM gains retained in the OE numerator would inflate the anchor, while sustainable cash funding net of CAS recoveries should determine the economic pension charge.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result, annual retiree benefit plan expense amounts for FAS are different from the amounts for CAS in any given reporting period even though the ultimate cost of providing benefits over the life of the plans is the same under each method.
audit_findings.explanation: The supplied record does not show the complete OE reconciliation, so contamination is not demonstrated. However, the $1.068 billion of accounting benefits equals about 61% of the $1.753 billion anchor OE and is plainly capable of changing the valuation. The different CAS expense, FAS service expense and actual contributions create a substantial double-counting or omission risk unless explicitly reconciled.
audit_findings.action: Produce the FY2025 OE pension reconciliation from GAAP net income through FAS service cost, non-operating benefit, MTM benefit, CAS recoveries and cash contributions; rerun after replacing accounting effects with a documented sustainable net cash pension cost.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter conflicts with an actual 2025 divestiture
audit_findings.magnitude: $231 million pre-tax gain, $333 million cash proceeds and $112 million of 2025 disposed-business sales; exact OE and lost-earnings impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The sale gain and pre-divestiture earnings can inflate anchor OE, while separately recognizing proceeds already contained in dated cash would double count the transaction in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: On May 24, 2025 (the “Divestiture date”), the company completed its previously announced sale of substantially all of the Immersive Mission Solutions (IMS) operating unit of Defense Systems (the “training services” business or “divestiture”) for $333 million in cash and recorded a pre-tax gain on sale of $231 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The null perimeter is demonstrably incorrect because the divestiture occurred. Whether the valuation itself is wrong remains unresolved because the OE reconciliation is absent. The $231 million gain equals 13.2% of anchor OE before tax, and the disposed business also contributed pre-sale operations, making the potential anchor distortion material even though the exact continuing-cost and tax effects are unknown.
audit_findings.action: Set the perimeter to reflect the May 24, 2025 divestiture; remove the $231 million gain and disposed-business earnings from OE, retain only continuing stranded costs, and reconcile the $333 million proceeds to the June 2026 cash balance so they enter value once.

audit_findings.title: Uncommenced leases are outside the reported lease-liability context
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.3 billion of filed rental commitments, compared with $2.188 billion of existing operating-lease liabilities at December 31, 2025; annual OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Rent enters future OE as the leases commence; associated facilities may also support the sales and growth assumed in the forecast.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we have approximately $1.3 billion in rental commitments for real estate leases that have not yet commenced.
audit_findings.explanation: These were future commitments rather than liabilities or full-year expenses in the 2025 anchor. Their value effect depends on commencement timing, replacement of existing facilities and incremental earnings generated, none of which is established. They are therefore a forward-looking forecast item to monitor rather than a demonstrated current valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Identify leases commenced by June and September 2026, annualize their rent, identify replaced facilities and link each lease to forecast capacity or revenue; revise forecast OE only for rent not matched by incremental earnings or avoided existing rent.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 residual $45 million ($1.472 billion filed D&A less $1.427 billion identified); all-eligible upper bound approximately $706 million or $4.95 per share in the bull scenario
audit_findings.mechanism: Eligible residual D&A would be added back to anchor OE, increasing operating value while leaving shares and the bridge unchanged.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2018 $580.0m (72.5% of filed D&A); FY2023 $1258.0m (94.0% of filed D&A); FY2025 $1427.0m (96.9% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: This is conservative rather than an overvaluation risk. The FY2025 residual is only 2.6% of anchor OE. Even assuming every residual dollar is eligible, the largest computed scenario effect is about $706 million, or 2.3% of bull equity value and $4.95 per share, which is insufficient to change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Classify the $45 million FY2025 residual using the fixed-asset and amortization schedules; rerun only for the portion supported as eligible non-economic D&A, without altering unidentified amounts.
